cards.explanation: The answer is mountains, friends. Jesus says, “…then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.” That's the whole direction, short and clear. I wish my recipes were that easy to follow.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “And let no one in the field return for his cloak.” The person working out in the field doesn't go back for it. I'd be standing there staring at my own apron, but that's the instruction.

The answer is pregnant and nursing mothers, friends. Jesus says, “How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!” I think this line hurts a little. Jesus names them, and it's good to slow down and notice who He names.

The answer is winter, friends. Jesus says, “Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.” He gives two things to pray about, and the season is the first one. Keep both in your head, bakers.

The answer is True. Jesus says there will be “…great tribulation, unseen from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be seen again.” Nothing like it has come before, and nothing like it will come after. That's a heavy line, so let it settle a second.

The answer is that those days will be cut short, friends. Jesus says, “But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.” And look at the line before it: if the days had not been cut short, nobody would be saved. That's the sentence to hang onto, bakers.

The answer is do not believe it, friends. Jesus says, “At that time, if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.” No chasing and no second-guessing. Sometimes the plainest instruction is the best one.

The answer is False. Jesus says false Christs and false prophets “…will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” So they do perform signs and wonders. A good show doesn't make it the real thing.

The answer is the elect, friends. Jesus says they will perform great signs and wonders “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” That little phrase, if that were possible, is worth noticing. It tells you how strong the deception will be.

The answer is lightning, friends. Jesus says, “For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.” East to west, all in one flash. That's a picture you won't forget.

The answer is that the stars will fall from the sky, friends. Jesus says, “the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.” The sun and moon go dark, and the stars fall. I'd be grabbing my hat for that.
The answer is on the clouds of heaven, friends. Jesus says, “They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” That's the picture He gives, and it's a big one.
The answer is angels, friends. Jesus says, “And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call…” They go out together with the trumpet. I think that's quite a sound.
The answer is True, friends. Jesus says the angels “…will gather His elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.” That's from every direction. Nobody gets missed.

The answer is that the branches turn tender and sprout leaves, friends. Jesus says, “As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.” Tender branches and new leaves are the signal. A fig tree never needs a timer.

The answer is that He is right at the door, friends. Jesus says, “So also, when you see all these things, you will know that He is near, right at the door.” Just like the leaves tell you summer is near. Near, bakers, not far.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.” Heaven and earth pass away, but His words don't. I'd stake my whole bakery on that, friends.
